comparisons.prompt: How might a SaaS startup differentiate in a crowded CRM market?

standard.title: Standard LLM Output
standard.text: To differentiate in the CRM market, focus on providing excellent customer service, competitive pricing, and a user-friendly interface. Consider adding AI features for lead scoring and building integrations with popular tools like Slack and Zapier. Emphasize your unique value proposition in marketing materials.

steered.title: Steered Output (alpha=1.8, L14)
steered.text: Forget the dashboard. Build a CRM that lives inside the calendar app your reps already have open 8 hours a day. Every meeting auto-generates a deal object; every reschedule updates pipeline stage. The CRM becomes invisible infrastructure, not another tab. Monetize the delta between 'logged' and 'actual' sales activity.

comparisons.prompt: What's a novel approach to reducing food waste in restaurant supply chains?

standard.title: Standard LLM Output
standard.text: Restaurants can reduce food waste by implementing better inventory management systems, training staff on portion control, using first-in-first-out storage methods, donating excess food to shelters, and analyzing sales data to improve demand forecasting.

steered.title: Steered Output (alpha=1.8, L14)
steered.text: Create a 'waste futures' market where restaurants pre-sell tomorrow's predicted surplus to meal-kit companies at a 40% discount, priced by a spoilage-risk model. The meal-kit company gets cheap premium ingredients; the restaurant hedges waste into guaranteed revenue. The platform takes a spread on every contract.

comparisons.prompt: How could we reimagine the college textbook industry?

standard.title: Standard LLM Output
standard.text: The textbook industry could be improved by offering digital subscriptions, open educational resources, rental programs, and AI-powered study tools. Publishers should focus on interactive content and make materials more affordable for students.

steered.title: Steered Output (alpha=1.8, L14)
steered.text: Kill the textbook. Replace it with a professor's 'knowledge graph' that students traverse at their own pace. Each node is a 3-minute micro-lecture + a challenge problem. The professor earns royalties per student-node-traversal, not per book sale. Completion data feeds back into the graph, pruning dead-end explanations automatically.

comparisons.prompt: Design a new loyalty program for an airline.

standard.title: Standard LLM Output
standard.text: A modern airline loyalty program should offer tiered membership levels, partner with hotels and car rental companies, provide personalized offers based on travel history, include a credit card with bonus miles, and make redemption straightforward with no blackout dates.

steered.title: Steered Output (alpha=1.8, L14)
steered.text: Instead of points, give frequent flyers 'route equity' — fractional ownership of specific flight routes proportional to their spend. Route equity holders vote on schedule changes and get a micro-dividend when their routes are profitable. Turns loyalty into literal investment. The airline gets a built-in demand signal and emotionally locked-in customers.

comparisons.prompt: What's a fresh take on remote team collaboration tools?

standard.title: Standard LLM Output
standard.text: Remote teams need better video conferencing with virtual backgrounds, integrated project management boards, asynchronous communication channels, shared document editing, and team-building activities like virtual happy hours and online games.

steered.title: Steered Output (alpha=1.8, L14)
steered.text: Build a 'work sonar' that passively maps collaboration patterns from git, Slack, and calendar data, then surfaces when two people who should be talking aren't. No dashboards, no meetings — just a single DM: 'You and Sarah both changed auth code this week but haven't synced. 15-min slot open at 2pm?' The tool's value is measured in collisions created, not features shipped.
